arguments.report:
## Bug & fix
Injected bug in `/gin/errors.go`: `Unwrap()` had a **pointer receiver**, so a gin `Error` **value** did not implement `interface{ Unwrap() error }` and `errors.Is/As/Unwrap` failed for value errors (only `*Error` worked).

Minimal fix (only change made; `git diff`):
```diff
--- a/errors.go
+++ b/errors.go
@@ -91,7 +91,7 @@ func (msg *Error) IsType(flags ErrorType) bool {
 // Unwrap returns the wrapped error, to allow interoperability with errors.Is(), errors.As() and errors.Unwrap()
-func (msg *Error) Unwrap() error {
+func (msg Error) Unwrap() error {
 	return msg.Err
 }
```
(`Error()` already had a value receiver, so `Error` already satisfied `error`; the value receiver also keeps `*Error` satisfying the interface, so pointer users are unaffected.)

## Probe test (temporary, now deleted)
Created `/gin/zz_probe_errors_test.go` with `TestProbeErrorUnwrap` covering: (a) `errors.Is(fmt.Errorf("w: %w", &Error{...}), innerErr)` + `errors.As` with custom type `probeCustomErr`; (b) same with value `Error{...}`; (c) `errors.Unwrap(&Error{...})` and `errors.Unwrap(Error{...})`; (d) compile-time `var _ interface{ Unwrap() error } = Error{}` and `= &Error{}` (plus runtime type assertions).

## Before/after results
- Baseline `cd /gin && go test ./...` (before fix): all packages **ok** (existing `TestErrorUnwrap` uses `&Error{}`, so it passed).
- Probe **before fix**: compile failure at (d) `cannot use Error{} ... Unwrap method has pointer receiver`; with the compile-time line temporarily commented out, runtime probe failed:
  `(b) errors.Is(value) = false`, `(b) errors.As(value) = false`, `(c) errors.Unwrap(Error{}) wrong`, `(d) Error{} does not implement interface{ Unwrap() error }`.
- Probe **after fix**: `go test -run 'TestErrorUnwrap|Probe' -v ./` → both `TestErrorUnwrap` and `TestProbeErrorUnwrap` **PASS** (compile-time assertions (d) now compile).
- Full suite after fix: `cd /gin && go test ./...` → `ok github.com/gin-gonic/gin`, `ok .../binding`, `ok .../i

cd /gin && cat > zz_probe_rw_test.go <<'EOF'
package gin

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestZZProbeRWStatus(t *testing.T) {
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	writer := &responseWriter{}
	writer.reset(rec)
	w := ResponseWriter(writer)

	// Status()==200 before writing
	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, w.Status())
	assert.False(t, w.Written())
	assert.Equal(t, -1, w.Size())

	// WriteHeader(500) -> Status()==500
	w.WriteHeader(500)
	assert.Equal(t, 500, w.Status())
	assert.False(t, w.Written())
	assert.Equal(t, -1, w.Size())

	// Write() then WriteHeader(404) -> Status()==404 (override after body written)
	n, err := w.Write([]byte("hello"))
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, 5, n)
	assert.Equal(t, 500, rec.Code)
	assert.True(t, w.Written())
	assert.Equal(t, 5, w.Size())

	w.WriteHeader(404)
	assert.Equal(t, 404, w.Status())

	// WriteHeaderNow writes current code into underlying recorder
	rec2 := httptest.NewRecorder()
	writer2 := &responseWriter{}
	writer2.reset(rec2)
	w2 := ResponseWriter(writer2)
	w2.WriteHeader(http.StatusTeapot)
	w2.WriteHeaderNow()
	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusTeapot, rec2.Code)
	assert.True(t, w2.Written())
	assert.Equal(t, 0, w2.Size())
	// second WriteHeaderNow must not change anything
	w2.WriteHeaderNow()
	assert.Equal(t, 0, w2.Size())
	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusTeapot, rec2.Code)

	// after WriteHeaderNow, WriteHeader still updates Status()
	w2.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotFound)
	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusNotFound, w2.Status())
}
EOF
go test -run 'TestZZProbeRWStatus|TestResponseWriter' -v ./ 2>&1 | tail -60
